A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Vlearn research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original Gymnasium and DMC continuous-control experiments, baseline comparisons, and Humanoid ablations in Section 4 and Figures 2–3.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments in Section 4 and Figures 2–4 and additionally reports qualitative hyperparameter-tuning findings in Appendix B.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same importance-weighted Bellman loss, TRPL policy updates, twin value critics, delayed updates, and importance-weight clipping. Algorithm 1 reformulates the loop and update conditions without establishing a different learning procedure.

E1.justification: Both evaluate Hopper-v4, Walker2D-v4, HalfCheetah-v4, Ant-v4, Humanoid-v4, and DMC dog-walk, dog-trot, and dog-run. The additional appendix discussion introduces no new evaluated task or environment.

E2.justification: The benchmark comparisons retain SAC, MPO, PPO, on-policy TRPL, and the one-step V-trace variant. The Humanoid component comparisons also retain the same alternatives; no evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Table 2 revises reported DMC MPO settings, including buffer size from 256 to 1e6, policy-update interval from 10000 to 1, and Polyak weight from 1 to 5e-3. These appear to correct misplaced entries; the PDFs do not establish reruns. Other benchmark protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The replay-buffer and component ablations are retained, moving from v1 Figure 2 to v2 Figure 4. Appendix B adds qualitative sensitivity observations about learning-rate/trust-region compatibility, batch size, and warm starts, without new quantitative ablation plots.

E5.justification: Both versions report ten seeds and means with 95% bootstrapped confidence intervals, including ten seeds for the buffer-size ablation. The new theoretical effective-sample-size discussion does not change empirical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: The benchmark and ablation curves are retained, as is the reported 25% Humanoid improvement over SAC. Appendix B newly reports that smaller batches worked better for Vlearn and off-policy V-trace and that warm-start samples provided no observed benefit.

T1.justification: v1 derives the bandit estimators but only expects squared importance weighting to have higher variance. v2 Appendix A.3 adds effective-sample-size definitions and an ordering argument, then asserts an unconditional variance ordering. This substantially strengthens the theoretical assertion, although its justification is incomplete. The original upper-bound and consistency proofs are retained.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains off-policy learning using only state-value critics. The revised abstract and introduction explicitly claim a nontrivial transfer of full-loss importance weighting to deep networks and promote the variance analysis and stabilizing design choices as contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix B newly interprets tuning behavior through the method's combination of on-policy and off-policy characteristics. The abstract also attributes twin critics to avoiding optimization bias, while the body retains the earlier regularization explanation. The substantive sample-efficiency and HalfCheetah limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds hyperparameter-search grids, best-configuration selection information, Nvidia V100 hardware, approximately 1–3 days of training, and software-source/license information. It also revises MPO table entries. Conversely, v1's reproducibility statement promising a camera-ready code release disappears; v2 supplies no Vlearn code-access replacement.

R1.justification: v2 more explicitly positions Vlearn as transferring established linear importance-weighting ideas to deep RL, adding discussion of TD(0) and LSTD. Added references include Bradtke and Barto, Graves and Ghiassian, Owen, and DMC/MuJoCo sources. The principal relationships to existing methods remain intact.

P1.justification: The abstract and substantial introductory, related-work, and explanatory passages are rewritten. Section 3 gains a separate estimator subsection and descriptive subheadings; appendices are reorganized, the reproducibility statement is removed, and the brief impact statement becomes an expanded Broader Impacts appendix.

P2.justification: The document changes from a two-column to a predominantly single-column layout, with redesigned title, author, equation, and algorithm placement. Figure 2's seven panels become five benchmark panels plus separate Figure 4 ablations. Plots are resized and relabeled, and both hyperparameter tables drop the redundant 'use critic' row.

improvement.justification: v2 improves reproducibility through search details, hardware/runtime disclosure, and corrected MPO entries, while clarifying prior-work attribution. However, Appendix A.3 strengthens v1's tentative variance intuition into a universal claim without establishing why an ordering based only on weights guarantees the reward-dependent estimator-variance ordering. The code-release commitment also disappears. These benefits and substantive qualification concerns leave the net quality change uncertain.
